subject: English Language

questions.prompt: What business brings income to many countries? (A terrorism, B industries, C tourism, D trade, E poaching)
steps: The included page 3 script names tourism.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which country receives many tourists yearly? (A Kenya, B Tanzania, C Uganda, D Malawi, E Zambia)
steps: The script explicitly names Tanzania.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which is a listed attraction pair? (A food/accommodation, B wildlife/transport, C high mountains/wildlife, D elephants/rivers, E beaches/money)
steps: The script lists wildlife, mountains, beaches, rivers and lakes.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: C. High mountains and wild animals is the direct general pair. D gives examples within the wider listed wildlife/rivers categories.

questions.prompt: Tourists spend on food and what? (A accommodation, B films, C TV, D radio, E clothes)
steps: The script names food, accommodation and transport.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Tanzania receives tourists every ___. (A month, B year, C week, D day, E Saturday)
steps: The script says every year.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Geffi ___ in Tanga for three years. (A has been, B have been living, C has been leaving, D have been leaving, E is been living)
steps: Geffi is singular and has been expresses the continuing period.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: They ___ water when visiting the Indian Ocean. (A seen, B see, C sees, D saw, E seed)
steps: A completed past visit uses saw.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Players ___ preparing for the game. (A is, B are, C have, D has, E will)
steps: Plural players takes are plus ing.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Lanta ___ been writing for an hour. (A does, B do, C did, D has, E will)
steps: Has been writing is the singular present perfect continuous.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: My nephew ___ for the exam last year. (A will sit, B will seat, C sat, D sited, E seated)
steps: Sat is the past tense of sit.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Seeds were ___ in November. (sewed, sown)
steps: Sown is the participle for planting seeds; sewed concerns stitching.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Yesterday the tyre ___ on the highway. (burst, busted)
steps: Burst is the standard past form for a tyre suddenly breaking open.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Several hens ___ their eggs under the cellar. (lie, lays)
steps: A plural subject takes lay; lie is intransitive and lays is singular.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: No correct option. Correct: lay their eggs.

questions.prompt: Last month ___ my foot against a chair. (hit, hited)
steps: Hit has unchanged past tense; hited is incorrect.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: Hit is the verb answer; the sentence also needs subject I.

questions.prompt: The carriage was ___ by six donkeys. (drawn, driven)
steps: Drawn means pulled by the animals.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match virtue: A reliable, B honesty/strong moral principles, C truthful, D good moral quality, E right/wrong principles.
steps: Virtue is a positive moral quality.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: D. A good moral quality in a person.

questions.prompt: Match moral.
steps: Moral concerns right and wrong.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: E. A principle about right and wrong behaviour.

questions.prompt: Match trustworthy.
steps: Trustworthy means reliable.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A. Someone you can trust and rely on.

questions.prompt: Match honest.
steps: Honest means telling the truth.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Match integrity.
steps: Integrity involves consistent moral conduct.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: B. Honesty and strong moral principles.

questions.prompt: What is a person who sings songs called?
steps: Singer is formed from sing plus er.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is a president's official residence called?
steps: In Tanzania the official residence is State House, Ikulu.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What is a place where people receive treatment called?
steps: Both provide treatment; hospital is the common intended answer.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Which class follows Standard Six?
steps: Seven follows six in the stated school sequence.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who controls an aircraft's flight?
steps: The pilot operates the aircraft.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Read aloud the following printed poem extract (Stieno is a source typo for Atieno): Atieno washes dishes, / Atieno plucks the chicken, / Atieno gets up early, / Beds her sacks down in the kitchen, / Atieno eight years old, / Atieno yo. / Since she is my sister’s child, / Stieno needs no pay, / While she works my wife can sit, / Sewing every sunny day, / With her earnings I support, / Atieno yo.
steps: Look at each printed word or letter carefully and say it in its printed order.
Blend sounds into words; for sentences, pause at punctuation. A teacher should assess pronunciation and fluency, rather than a different written answer.
questions.answer: Oral response: Atieno washes dishes, / Atieno plucks the chicken, / Atieno gets up early, / Beds her sacks down in the kitchen, / Atieno eight years old, / Atieno yo. / Since she is my sister’s child, / Stieno needs no pay, / While she works my wife can sit, / Sewing every sunny day, / With her earnings I support, / Atieno yo.

questions.prompt: Who speaks in the Atieno extract?
steps: He calls her my sister's child and mentions my wife, supporting the uncle interpretation.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Who is the person described?
steps: Her name is repeated throughout.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: How old is Atieno in this extract?
steps: The first stanza directly gives her age.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Where does she sleep?
steps: The line about bedding her sacks down gives this place and bedding.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: What does Atieno yo represent in the poem?
steps: Identify its repeated structural role; the extract does not provide a literal translation of yo.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.
questions.answer: A refrain: the repeated line at the end of each stanza, keeping attention on Atieno.

questions.prompt: Order A-E: Bura signals Ami to stand still and be silent.
steps: The protective gesture follows their fear.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: The lion looks at them then goes away.
steps: The departure ends the encounter.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Ami and Bura travel together through the forest.
steps: Introduce the travellers and setting.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: Both are terrified and do not know what to do.
steps: Fear follows appearance of the lion.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

questions.prompt: Order: A huge lion bursts from a nearby bush.
steps: The sudden appearance triggers their reaction.
Use this rule or evidence to write the answer below.

summaries.Listening and grammar: Listen to the supplied teacher text and identify the exact detail asked for. Check spelling and sentence punctuation; missing scripts are explicitly identified.
summaries.Vocabulary: Use sentence meaning, subject agreement and time clues to choose the word or verb form. Apply the specific rule explained for each task and note ambiguous choices.
summaries.Oral reading: Read aloud in the printed order. Pronounce words clearly and pause at punctuation. Teachers assess accuracy and fluency; the printed text is the oral response.
summaries.Poetry and composition: Find evidence in the passage or poem before answering. Distinguish explicit statements, reasonable inferences and model interpretations.

references.title: CITIZEN Standard Six Set 11 Examinations 2025 Citizen Pre & Primary School

limitations: 3(iii): Neither lie nor singular lays fits plural hens; lay is required.
3(iv): Subject I is missing and hited is an incorrect form.
6: Stieno in stanza two is a typo for Atieno.
6(v): Refrain is the literary function; no literal translation of yo is supplied.
